thread:
lina: Heads-up — planning a small routing change at 21:00 UTC today to prime the regional fallback weights for eu-west and apac. This is NOT a full cutover, just a gentle weight nudge + TTL lower for faster handback. Will take ~15-20m.

lina: Goal: make sure fallback policy (when a region drops) routes to the secondary region predictably and TTL propagation is fast during the quiet window.

sam: timeline ok for me. who’s owning the actual weight flip and smoke?

arjun: I can run the smoke checks and watch metrics. I'll be on-call and in the channel at T-10m.

tess: I’ll do the orchestrated weight updates via rbctl, and hold the rollback commands ready.

lina: thanks — plan:
- 20:50 UTC: deploy-bot will announce quiet window
- 20:55 UTC: lower DNS TTLs for eu edge from 300 -> 60s (one zone at a time)
- 21:00 UTC: set weight eu-west=85, apac=15 (priming step)
- 21:05 UTC: smoke checks + traffic sanity (arjun)
- 21:10-21:15 UTC: observe for 10m, then either return to baseline or continue next step

lina: rollback plan (if anything looks off):
- rbctl set-weight eu-west 100 apac 0
- restore TTLs to 300s
- open incident if errors > 1% latency filter or 5xx spike > 0.5% for 5m

arjun: smoke checklist I’ll run:
1) curl-based end-to-end check against primary region endpoint:
```
curl -sS -H "x-test-client: smoke" https://edge-api.redwood.internal/health | jq .status
```
2) sampling SLOs: 95p latency, 5xx rate via metrics query
3) verify KV cache hit rates unchanged (no cache storms)
4) quick replay of a few representative requests via test harness

sam: small ask — can we also validate DNS from a few public resolvers (8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1) and from our eur-ops jumpbox? DNS can be weird with staggered CDN caches.

tess: yep — running these from jumpbox:
```
dig +short edge.redwood.net @8.8.8.8
dig +short edge.redwood.net @1.1.1.1
```
I'll post diffs.

deploy-bot: Quiet window scheduled: 20:50 UTC -> 21:30 UTC. Please set presence to DND if you are not part of the change.

ops-watch: I’ll be watching synthetic checks and the routing-health dashboard. If route failovers > 2 in 10m, I’ll ping on-call and set a block.

lina: small caveat — we're only priming fallback weights today. No model or runtime changes. This is low-risk but still want eyes.

arjun: If smoke looks green, do we plan a second step to push apac to 25% in the next window?

tess: We'll discuss after observation. For today, keep it conservative.

sam: two operational notes:
- ensure canary path has rate limit exception so our smoke hits are not throttled
- annotate the route change in the change log with the rbctl command used

lina: RB commands (I’ll paste into the change log before we run):
```
rbctl set-weight eu-west 85 && rbctl set-weight apac 15 && rbctl annotate "priming fallback weights: eu-west->85 apac->15"
```

lina: after the change, please paste these three things to the thread:
- smoke curl output (one-liner)
- dig output snapshot
- any metric snapshots (5xx, p50/p95 latency)

arjun: noted. I’ll also run a quick stability script that replays 50 requests across both regions and dump results.

tess: I’ll push the rbctl commands at 21:00 exactly and confirm when done.

deploy-bot: Change executed by tess at 21:00: rbctl set-weight eu-west 85 apac 15.

tess: done. confirmed slight bump in apac inbound on our flow logs. posting dig and smoke now.

arjun: smoke: {"status":"ok"} p95=180ms p50=40ms 5xx=0.02% :thumbsup:

tess: dig results: 8.8.8.8 -> 52.11.99.12, 1.1.1.1 -> 52.11.99.12, jumpbox -> 52.18.2.7

ops-watch: metrics look stable. no route failovers, 5xx < 0.1% across the board.

sam: good. I'm toggling the TTL restore script to run at 21:20 if everything stays green.

lina: solid. if anything regresses, run rollback commands on this thread and mark as incident-open. otherwise we’ll leave primed and revisit weight step next week.

arjun: leaving notes in the runbook and closing my watch in 30m. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
